deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to lecture notes on natural philosophy and mechanics. The previous page derives Gauss's principle of least constraint. The next page develops Clausius's mechanical theory of heat: dQ = U dv + V dt, an integrating factor λ, and a Carnot cycle K1, K2. This page is the bridge between the two.

(1) Energy conservation for a conservative mechanical system: T + U = const, with T the kinetic and U the potential energy. Riemann labels this 'Satz von der Erhaltung der lebendigen Kraft' (conservation of vis viva).

(2) He then states the 'Satz von der Erhaltung der Kraft' (Helmholtz's term) as a hypothesis. The work done by the forces between material particles is zero whenever all particles return to the same relative positions and velocities. In modern terms, the internal forces do no net work over any closed cycle of configurations, so a potential (internal energy) exists.

(3) Application to heat. The work done in the relative (internal, molecular) motion of the particles equals the heat supplied to the body. The work done in the motion of the body element as a whole is to be added; this sentence is left unfinished. The marginal remark 'gleiche Temperatur, immer die Wärmemenge' reads: same temperature, always the same quantity of heat, i.e. the heat is a function of the state. This is the first law, in a form where heat is identified with the internal work of the particles.

(4) Notation after the rule: Q is the heat supplied to a body. The state variables are pressure and temperature. The external work is p dv. The heat differential is written dQ = M dv + N dt, with v the volume and t the temperature. This is Clausius's form, taken up on the next page as dQ = U dv + V dt with U = p/A.

(5) Hydrodynamics. The Euler momentum equation in the x-direction, without body force, is
-∂p/∂x = ρ(∂u/∂t + u ∂u/∂x + v ∂u/∂y + w ∂u/∂z).
Riemann rewrites it in conservation (divergence) form. The exact identity (my completion) is
ρ Du/Dt = ∂(ρu)/∂t + ∂(ρu²)/∂x + ∂(ρuv)/∂y + ∂(ρuw)/∂z − u[∂ρ/∂t + ∂(ρu)/∂x + ∂(ρv)/∂y + ∂(ρw)/∂z].
He writes the first group above a rule and the correction terms u ∂(ρu)/∂x + u ∂(ρv)/∂y + u ∂(ρw)/∂z below it, to be subtracted. He then writes the continuity equation
∂ρ/∂t + ∂(ρu)/∂x + ∂(ρv)/∂y + ∂(ρw)/∂z = 0.
This kills the bracket and gives the conservation form
-∂p/∂x = ∂(ρu)/∂t + ∂(ρu²)/∂x + ∂(ρuv)/∂y + ∂(ρuw)/∂z.
The purpose is presumably the energy or heat balance of a moving fluid element: work of the pressure p dv, combined with dQ, as in his 1860 gas-dynamics paper, which uses conservation forms.
errors: In the conservation-form expression the z-term is written ∂(ρvw)/∂z; it must be ∂(ρuw)/∂z. The image may also show ∂(ρuw)/∂y where ∂(ρuv)/∂y is needed. These are slips in the velocity letters.
The subtracted correction line omits the term u ∂ρ/∂t. The full bracket multiplying u is the whole continuity expression ∂ρ/∂t + div(ρ𝐯).
The correction terms are written with '+' signs below a rule; they must be subtracted. Most likely the rule is meant as subtraction layout, but as written the sign is ambiguous.
The sentence 'Die bei der Bewegung ... des Körperelements geleistete Arbeit —' is left incomplete.

Equating the heat supplied with the work done in the relative motion of the particles alone, without separating the external work p dv, is a loose statement of the first law. The next page corrects this with A Q = A U + W.

results.what: T + U = const for conservative systems (conservation of vis viva)
results.usually_credited_to: Leibniz/Huygens (vis viva); Lagrange in general form

results.what: Conservation of force as the hypothesis that internal forces do zero work over a closed cycle of relative configurations and velocities
results.modern_name: energy conservation / existence of an internal-energy potential (first law)

results.what: dQ = M dv + N dt with external work p dv
results.modern_name: first law of thermodynamics in Clausius's differential form

results.what: Euler momentum equation rewritten in conservation form using the continuity equation
results.modern_name: conservative (divergence) form of the momentum equation
results.usually_credited_to: Euler 1757 (equations); the conservation form is standard 19th-century material

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard lecture-note materials: energy conservation, Helmholtz's conservation of force, Clausius's dQ, and the conservation form of Euler's equations. Riemann's use of conservation-form gas dynamics is already known from his 1860 shock-wave paper.

checkable.asserts: Equals 0: ρ Du/Dt equals the conservative flux form minus u times the continuity expression.
Nonzero in general: confirms that Riemann's written term ∂(ρvw)/∂z is a slip for ∂(ρuw)/∂z.

transcription_corrections: The z-term in the image reads ∂(ρvw)/∂z, a slip for ∂(ρuw)/∂z. The y-term in the image appears to be ∂(ρuw)/∂y rather than ∂(ρuv)/∂y.
The second line of the momentum identity starts with '+ +' (or a stray mark) under a horizontal rule; it is a subtraction layout, not an additive continuation.
'Die bei der Bewegung [...] des Körperelements geleistete Arbeit' ends with a dash ('—'), not '='.
The marginal '+' before 'Gleiche Temperatur' is a cross-shaped mark; the line ends with '.—', not '='.
